explanation: Chlorine has a higher electron affinity than Fluorine. Although Fluorine is more electronegative, its very small atomic size causes strong inter-electronic repulsion when an electron is added, reducing the energy released. Chlorine's larger size reduces this repulsion, giving it the highest electron affinity among halogens.
stem: Which halogen has the highest electron affinity (most energy released when gaining an electron)?

explanation: A more reactive halogen (higher oxidizing power) displaces a less reactive halide ion from its salt. Chlorine is a stronger oxidizing agent than Bromine, so $Cl_2$ can displace $Br^-$: $Cl_2 + 2KBr \rightarrow 2KCl + Br_2$.
